summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: How to Create Bandages in MD ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to create bandages in Marvelous Designer (MD). The process is simple and involves using basic shapes and tools within the software. ## Getting Started First, open Marvelous Designer and find a VR male model. Double-click to enter the working area in the virtual model file housed in the window of the library. ## Setting Up the Model To show the model directly, switch the display type of the model to black and white surface. Select the rectangle tool in the drop-down menu on the menu bar. ### Creating the Rectangle Create a rectangle with dimensions of 20x200. Click on the positioning tool in the upper right corner and then click on the virtual model to place it near the model. ### Adjusting the Rectangle To compare the dimensions, if the width seems too narrow, open the panel along the side. Quickly adjust the line by deleting any excess straight lines. If it still appears narrow, drag the side to widen the panel. ### Line Adjustment During the process of moving the line, press the Shift key to move along the reference line. You can also press the right mouse button to enter specific numbers for precise adjustments. ## Editing the Texture Use the edit texture tool to check the gold tail of the panel. Since we want to shrink the panel horizontally, we need to shrink it in the direction of the arrowhead, which involves reducing the tail shrink. ## Preparing for Simulation Before adding the fixer tool, ensure to reduce the particle diameter. Open the simulation; the panel will hang on the hand. To observe the effect more clearly, change the fabric color first. ### Observing the Fit After rotating the view, we can see that the band should fit the human body. However, there is some distance between the model and the panel. Reducing the conflict thickness can help minimize the air thickness around the panel. #### Conflict Thickness Conflict thickness is a property that produces instability, preventing the grid from getting too close to the top. After opening the simulation again, observe that the panel is closer to the human body. ## Final Adjustments At this point, there is still a gap between the panel and the human body due to air thickness, known as the surface diameter. You can modify the surface diameter of the entire model to achieve a better fit. ### Adding Fixed Needles To add a fixed needle at both ends and adjust the band, keep the two ends of the line as straight as possible. Harden the panel so that it cannot bend easily, helping maintain the shape of the two ends. Select the fixed needle tool and add a fixed needle along one side of the panel line to the top of the grid. Ensure not to bend the position of the double needle again. If you need to delete a fixed needle, select it and press Delete. ### Simulation of the Panel Open the simulation to let the panel drop naturally. The first grid may be relatively large; thus, even after reducing the particle diameter, it might still not be as fine as needed. Try reducing the particle diameter to 8 and simulate again. ## Repeat Operations To prevent the transformation of the grid from re-placing, delete the fixed needle and repeat the process. As the cloth pin gets closer to your finger, you may notice some bulging. You can reduce the particle diameter further to 5. ### Enhancing the Fabric Continue to repeat the process and increase the friction needle. Repeat the hardening plate and add a fixed needle. After removing the hardening, open the simulation again to allow the fabric to fall naturally and hang on the hand. ## Positioning the Fixed Needle Select the middle position of the fixed needle and click to set a standard. By rotating and moving the fixed needle, ensure it is close to the hand position for a smoother attachment of the fabric. ### Fixing the Needle to the Model After adjusting the angle, confirm the fixed needle is close to the hand. Select the fixed needle function in the right-click menu, then the fixed needle will be anchored to the virtual model grid, preventing movement. ## Working with the 3D Window Open the simulation again in a point where the movement of the 2D window is not fixed. The 3D window will remain stable as the fixed needle is secured. ### Observing Movement and Rotation In the 3D window, the fabric will be attracted as you move it. Continue to move and rotate the fixed needle to develop the fiber, being mindful not to stretch it excessively, especially during movement. ## Using the Hand Strap Next, we will use the hand strap to ensure the fabric wraps evenly around the palm. Pull the board by hand to attach it to the palm evenly. ### Ensuring Proper Attachment The strap should hold the board on the palm instead of the palm itself. As previously mentioned, rotate the fixing needle occasionally to ensure the board adheres smoothly to the palm. ## Managing Multi-layer Intersection After multi-layer intersection and entanglement, the board may slide together, affecting the simulation. Increasing friction can prevent the fabric from sliding and create better folds. ### Adjusting the Fabric When the friction coefficient is low, the fabric tends to slide. While entangling, ensure the fixing needle is hidden at the model's endpoint. This will require repeating the previous operation carefully. ## Sewing the Fabric If you want the fabric to stick together, you can use a sewing needle. Select the sewing needle tool, click on the two fabrics, and complete the sewing. The sewing needle tool does not lower the total into the entire area of the piece. ### Finalizing the Setup You can approach other fabrics gradually through the fixed needle, integrating the end material of the band into the already entangled parts. Stop the simulation, hide the virtual model, and fix the fixed pin to the virtual model. ## Adjusting the Band Position Drag and drop to cover the endpoint. Remove the fixed pin and readjust the position of the band. After setting everything up, reattach it to the virtual model. ## Creating Folds in the Band Now, we will begin working on the details of the band folds. Since our fabric has always been shrunk, it is narrower than desired. Add a fixed pin and double-click to fix the fabric's position on both sides. ### Setting the Reduced Shrink Increase the reduced shrink to 90, which will cause significant changes in the material in the middle, forming the desired folds. You may increase it to 100, but this may create too many folds; adjust based on your preference. ### Final Adjustments for Folds I have chosen a reduced shrink of 85. If you want thinner folds, you can change the particle diameter to 3, especially since the size of this panel is relatively small. After simulating, you'll see that the folds become more detailed. ## Addressing Protrusions If there are protrusions on the side of the panel due to the absence of a fixed pin on the newly added grid, double-click to control the grid and do a short simulation. This will ensure that the folds maintain their shape throughout the simulation process. ### Using Shape Optimization If you encounter conflicts or instability due to shape optimization, use the multiple shape optimization function. First, cancel the shape optimization of the panel. Utilize the grid brush tool to select the shape optimization area. ### Partial Shape Optimization After selecting the area, perform partial shape optimization to stabilize any unstable parts. The folds of the palm part will remain self-formed without needing optimization. ## Conclusion This concludes the tutorial. Thank you for following along, and see you in the next video! ```
